description:
SaS Twilight is a solo team driven by curiosity, creativity and a passion for space exploration. This year, I chose "Abandoned but not Forgotten" to uncover the stories behind equipment left on the Moon and Mars. Through research and storytelling, I aim to show how these forgotten objects represent human ingenuity, scientific progress and our journey into the unknown. 
Beyond the Twilight, Every Forgotten Object Has a Story
summary:
The Last Footprints: A Journey Through Humanity's Forgotten Space Explorers** is an educational science-fiction comic book that explores the stories of NASA's spacecraft, rovers, landers and scientific instruments left behind across the Solar System.

Through 18 illustrated pages, readers follow ORBIT, a curious exploration robot, on an exciting journey across the Moon, Mars, asteroids and deep space. Along the way, ORBIT discovers historical explorers such as the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicles, Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Ingenuity, Dawn and Pioneer spacecraft. The comic explains their original missions, scientific discoveries and current status through engaging storytelling and visually appealing illustrations.

This project addresses the challenge by transforming complex NASA historical and scientific information into an accessible, entertaining and educational narrative for school-age students and space enthusiasts. It is important because it highlights the achievements of past space missions, demonstrates how abandoned space technology contributed to scientific progress, and inspires the next generation to explore science, technology and the mysteries of the universe.

**Although these explorers may have fallen silent, their discoveries continue to shape humanity's future.**
details:
The Last Footprints is an educational comic book that introduces readers to NASA's spacecraft, rovers, landers and scientific instruments that remain in space or on other celestial bodies. Through 18 illustrated pages, readers follow ORBIT, a small exploration robot, as it travels across the Moon, Mars, asteroids and deep space. Each chapter introduces a different space mission, explaining its purpose, achievements, discoveries and current status through storytelling, dialogue and illustrations.
The comic transforms complicated scientific and historical information into an engaging and easy-to-understand learning experience. It encourages students to develop an interest in astronomy, space exploration, science and technology. It also helps readers understand that even missions that have ended can continue to contribute valuable scientific knowledge.
The project aims to raise awareness of humanity's past space exploration efforts and inspire the next generation to learn more about the universe. It also highlights the importance of scientific research, technological innovation and the knowledge gained from previous missions.
Artificial intelligence tools such as Google Gemini were used to generate illustrations based on carefully prepared prompts. The comic's pages, dialogue and educational content were developed and organised using digital writing and design tools.
Instead of presenting NASA information in a traditional textbook format, the project combines science education with science-fiction storytelling. ORBIT serves as the central guide, connecting different missions into one continuous adventure. The illustrations, conversations and journey-based structure make historical space missions more memorable and enjoyable.
We considered scientific accuracy, historical information, readability, visual consistency and the target audience. Special attention was given to ensuring that the spacecraft and scientific instruments were represented as accurately as possible. The team also maintained a consistent character design for ORBIT and used simple yet informative dialogue to make the content accessible to young readers.
